newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ANI moves against rebel committee.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ANI moves against rebel committee.

text.p: Engineering group Australian National Industries Ltd (ANI) said on Monday it had revoked the power of a board committee which was inquiring into ANI's purchase of the Holter environmental group in Germany and had appointed lawyer Robert Ellicott to handle the inquiries.
The company said Ellicott's appointment was approved by a majority of the ANI board.
"I expect that Mr Ellicott's appointment will bring to an end extensive recent speculation which has not been in the company's interest," chairman Ted Harris said.
The ANI statement did not say if the two directors who were members of the committee, Ross Palmer and Fred Smith, voted in favour of Ellicott's appointment.

"I anticipate that the enquiry of the ABT matters will proceed under Mr Ellicott's guidance untrammelled by other distractions which are personally being played out, in and out of the board room, and that a full independent report will be made to the board as soon as those enquiries have been completed to the satisfaction of the external advisers and Mr Ellicott, QC," the chairman said.
